page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a baseline frequency of 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks AVX-512 support.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2697.99, placing it in the top 25% tier. Multi-core CPU performance and memory read bandwidth remain within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 10782.37 and cached small-block read speeds of 516.94 GB/sec. However, certain resource bottlenecks are present. Large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is weak at 18.88 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% tier. Additionally, while the instance handles light LLM tasks adequately, prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak at 17.15 tokens/sec, indicating a performance tradeoff for larger computational workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c7a.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of local storage or high memory allocations. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate text or image processing. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-effective choice for stateless application tiers, CI/CD pipelines, and microservices that offload storage and acceleration to external cloud services.
